method: Conservative direct review of candidate labels and their recorded aliases against benchmark gold; this is a terminology audit, not a blinded clinical diagnostic adjudication.

cases.gold: Catatonia related to underlying Lewy body dementia
cases.assessment: Component/parent labels omit the causal composite; neither alone is clinical-complete. The candidate list separately contains DLB, but no composite label.
Disjunction of individual components is not the composite diagnosis; PAH also lacks idiopathic scope. No exact composite candidate label.
Disease family is relevant but lacks the specified subtype; the sole old and v2 common top1 success is not complete at full-label granularity.
Unspecified abscess is a parent diagnosis; location and communicating-space morphology omitted. No exact full candidate label.
Exact disease label; legacy membership is appropriate for this label.
Recorded alias supplies intended equivalence, but lowercase Neuralgic amyotrophy is also present and omitted from membership. Broader plexitis labels should not automatically be merged.
First label is complete. Appendicitis is a parent and its stored alias Appendiceal stump appendicitis is a granularity conflation.

Carcinoma is a broad parent. The explicit candidate Sarcomatoid squamous cell carcinoma is a strong full-entity equivalent and is absent from legacy membership. Sarcomatoid Carcinoma/Spindle cell carcinoma require an explicit context-sensitive equivalence judgment.
Case-only duplicates refer to the full disease label; membership is appropriate although duplicate candidate slots affect binding/ranking.

Wrong entity, not merely a parent. In method_hypothesis_recall_48.jsonl multistance concept C06 is labeled Hemangioma but aliases include Hemangiosarcoma and Angiosarcoma. build_trial_tasks inherited gold_match=strong. This is concept/alias corruption; no safe clinical equivalence can be inferred from these aliases.
Manifestation-only label omits causal attribution; no full causal target in the explicit candidate labels.
